sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Amelanchier ovalis is a deciduous shrub or small tree, usually 1–3 m in French field accounts but reaching 6 m in some horticultural references. It grows on rocky slopes, cliffs and sunny calcareous ground. Its toothed oval leaves are white-felted beneath when young; white five-petalled flowers appear in spring racemes. Small fruits change from red to blue-black.

sections.title: Food and identification
sections.text: The ripe fruits are edible pomes, though one horticultural source describes them as not especially palatable. The common name snowy mespilus is also applied to other Amelanchier in cultivation, so the Latin name helps identify this European species.
